I.1|cover|File:Astronaut Riding a Horse.description: This is a digital composite or manipulated photograph, not a traditional painting, drawing, or diagram. It depicts an astronaut in a white NASA spacesuit with an American flag patch riding a white horse across a barren, gray lunar-like surface, with Earth’s blue atmosphere and clouds visible in the background against the blackness of space. No person’s face is clearly identifiable — the astronaut’s helmet visor is reflective gold and obscures any facial features. There is no visible text in the image.
I.1|cover|File:Astronaut Riding a Horse.brief: Stable Diffusion 3.5 still of an astronaut on a horse (2024 demo image): a generative digital image that makes the unit's claim visible — fashion and commercial images are now also machine-made files.

I.1|analysis-model|File:Dirty and damage.description: This is a photograph of a small doll with a bald head, painted facial features including blue eyeshadow and defined eyebrows, and wispy gray hair. The doll wears a pink knitted top and is positioned in front of a white lace-trimmed garment or fabric, with a thin green stem crossing diagonally in the foreground. No person’s face is clearly identifiable as human; the subject is an artificial doll. There is no visible text in the image.
I.1|analysis-model|File:Dirty and damage.brief: A dirty, damaged fashion doll photographed as an object: material wear and staging that students can describe before interpreting fashion's ideal body.

I.1|masterclass-1|File:Dorothy Lamour -.description: This is a vintage black-and-white print advertisement featuring a photograph of a smiling woman with dark, curled hair wearing a leopard-print coat, seated next to a man whose face is partially visible in profile. The ad contains extensive text promoting "Woodbury Complete Beauty Cream," including the headline "this One Complete Cream is all you need!" and a caption identifying the woman as "Dorothy Lamour soon to be seen in 'ROAD TO UTOPIA,' a Paramount Picture." A small inset image shows a hand holding a jar of the cream, and the brand name "Woodbury" is prominently displayed in script at the bottom.
I.1|masterclass-1|File:Dorothy Lamour -.brief: 1945 Woodbury Complete Beauty Cream advertisement with Dorothy Lamour: a commercial beauty still showing how fashion imagery sells a practice, not only a garment.

I.1|masterclass-2|File:Lautrec the photo.description: This is a vintage printed advertisement or poster, likely from the late 19th or early 20th century, featuring stylized line art and flat color blocks on a pale yellow-green background. It depicts a woman in an elaborate red dress with a mask on the left, and a man operating a large box camera on a tripod on the right, with a small figure of a woman walking a dog in the far background. The visible text includes “9. Place Pigalle” at the top, “P. Sescau” in large red letters below the camera, and “Photographe” beneath that, along with a small black elephant logo next to the name. No person’s face is clearly identifiable — the woman wears a mask, and the man’s face is obscured by the camera he is looking through.
I.1|masterclass-2|File:Lautrec the photo.brief: Toulouse-Lautrec, poster for photographer Sescau, 1894: a print that already treats photography as a commercial service — the fashion image is not 'just a file format'.

I.1|masterclass-3|File:Illustrated fashi.description: This is a black-and-white printed page, likely from a vintage catalog or advertisement, featuring six illustrated women in formal 19th-century dresses. The image is divided into two sections with the headings "READY MADE WASH SUITS" and "READY MADE WHITE SUITS," each showing three figures labeled with figure numbers (Fig. 63 through Fig. 68) and detailed descriptions of the garments along with prices. The illustrations are detailed line drawings, not photographs, and while the women's faces are depicted, they are stylized and not clearly identifiable as specific individuals.
I.1|masterclass-3|File:Illustrated fashi.brief: Illustrated fashion catalogue page, summer 1890: several garment genres (day, promenade, evening) printed side by side on one plate — many fashion genres at once.

I.1|masterclass-4|File:Beauty is my busi.description: This is a vintage print advertisement, likely from a magazine, featuring a color illustration of a smiling woman with red hair and a green headband, wearing a light-colored dress. The ad contains prominent text including the headline "Beauty is my business," the brand name "SweetHeart Soap," and phrases like "Adorable Cover Girl" and "9 out of 10 Cover Girls use SWEETHEART's new Large Bath Size." While the woman’s face is clearly depicted and stylized, she is not identifiable as a specific real person; the ad also includes small illustrations of two babies in a tub and handwritten-style script elements.
I.1|masterclass-4|File:Beauty is my busi.brief: 1950 magazine still 'Beauty is my business, says Anne Piron': a working beauty professional framed for commerce — art and commerce share the same page.

I.1|masterclass-5|File:Art+Feminism Wiki.description: This is a photograph showing a person holding a book titled "Rising to the Occasion" by Rebecca Belmore, published by Vancouver Art Gallery. No faces are clearly identifiable in the image.
I.1|masterclass-5|File:Art+Feminism Wiki.brief: Art+Feminism Wikipedia Edit-A-Thon 2015, Banff: editors gathered around screens, a public circulation moment where who writes the image record becomes visible.

I.1|masterclass-6|File:Fan SAAM-1935.8.2.description: This is a photograph of a traditional Japanese folding fan (sensu) with a painted design. The fan features a light green and cream-colored paper surface decorated with delicate purple and white flowers, possibly irises or similar blooms, along with green leaves and stems. The wooden ribs of the fan are visible at the bottom, fanning out from a central pivot point, and the edges of the paper appear to be gilded or have a golden trim. There is no visible text on the fan, and no person's face is identifiable in the image.
I.1|masterclass-6|File:Fan SAAM-1935.8.2.brief: Smithsonian American Art Museum Chinese export fan (SAAM 1935.8.20): an object whose painted scene and museum credit line force the question of who counts in the archive.

I.1|lab-1|File:Miss Maquillage Digital F.description: This is a side-by-side comparison of two photographs featuring the same woman in different outfits, standing outdoors against a backdrop of green trees and a paved area. Her face is clearly visible and identifiable in both images.

No person's face is clearly identifiable in the image.

I.2|masterclass-1|File:Costumes civils H.description: This is a colorized historical print or diagram titled "COSTUMES CIVILS" at the top, which displays numerous figures in period clothing arranged in horizontal rows to illustrate the evolution of French civilian fashion from the reign of Louis XIV through the early 20th century. The image includes labels for different eras and social classes, such as "Gens de qualité," "Révolution," and "Second Empire," along with specific years like 1815, 1830, and 1925. I.2|masterclass-2|File:Vector graphic sc.description: This image is a digital illustration or graphic design, not a photograph, painting, or document. It features a stylized, abstract composition with four quadrants: the top-left shows a yellow circle with an orange crescent and a small brownish oval shape; the top-right displays a large, ornate, egg-like form with a white border and brown interior against a yellow background with radiating lines; the bottom-left contains angular brown and tan shapes resembling cracked earth or rock; and the bottom-right shows a dark brown curved shape over an orange field. There is no visible text, and no person’s face is identifiable in any part of the image.

I.2|masterclass-3|The composite capital.description: This is a black-and-white architectural drawing or print, likely from a book or technical manual, illustrating the design of a Corinthian capital. It features multiple views including a front elevation, a plan view (top-down), and a three-dimensional perspective rendering of the ornate column top with its characteristic acanthus leaves and volutes. Visible text includes "FIG. XXV." in the upper right corner and labels such as "M2" and "P2" near the diagrams. No person's face is identifiable in the image.
I.2|masterclass-3|The composite capital.brief: Composite capital drawn in perspective (NYPL plate): a technique taught inside a concrete architectural problem, not as abstract skill.

I.2|masterclass-4|File:The The Designer.description: This is a vintage magazine cover, likely a printed publication, featuring a painted illustration of a woman in profile wearing an ornate, light-colored dress, seated outdoors at night with a dark blue sky and trees in the background. The woman’s face is shown in profile but is not clearly identifiable as a specific individual; it is stylized and artistic rather than photographic or realistic.

I.2|masterclass-5|File:Vector graphic de.description: This graphic design was made for the free software promotional video entitled "Free/libre software: Free your creativity" (video made by the same author, published by Armaludis under CC BY-SA license).

I.2|masterclass-6|File:Raster graphic fi.description: This is a digital pixel art image, not a photograph, drawing, print, painting, diagram, or document. There is no visible text, and no person's face is identifiable in the image.

I.2|lab-1|File:CosmicBloom.jpg.description: This is a photograph of an art installation featuring several mannequins dressed in elaborate, avant-garde garments, including one with a large, circular, wire-frame skirt and another with a voluminous blue ruffled dress. I.2|lab-2|File:Surrealism (49679583271)..description: This is a black-and-white photograph of an abstract, geometric sculpture composed of interlocking rectangular blocks. There is no visible text, and no person's face is identifiable in the image.

I.2|lab-3|File:Work in Progress.JPG.description: This is a digital illustration or drawing that depicts an anime-style female character with pink hair, blue eyes, and fox-like ears and tail, wearing a dark blue outfit with white frills and a pink patterned top, sitting next to a small white cat with a red bow. I.3|cover|File:News kiosk -Exhibition of.description: This is a photograph of a glass-fronted display case filled with magazines and craft supplies. I.3|analysis-model|File:Dresses by Rei K.description: This is a photograph of an art installation or exhibition display featuring five mannequins dressed in elaborate, avant-garde black garments with sculptural headpieces. I.3|masterclass-1|File:CMYK.png.description: This is a digital graphic or print design, not a photograph, painting, or document. I.3|masterclass-2|File:Nokia 8-display p.description: This is a digital image or photograph of a close-up view of an LED display screen, showing a grid of individual red, green, and blue pixels against a black background. There is no visible text, and no person's face is identifiable in the image.

I.3|masterclass-3|Fashion illustration.description: This is a stylized illustration or print, likely from the early 20th century, depicting two women in elegant, patterned dresses standing on a balcony overlooking a body of water with a distant ship and swirling smoke or steam. The artwork features bold black outlines, flat areas of color (primarily blues, greens, and off-white), and decorative Art Deco or Art Nouveau influences in the railing design and flowing lines. There is no clearly identifiable person’s face — both figures are rendered with simplified, profile-like features — and the only visible text is a small monogram “R” in the lower right corner.

I.3|masterclass-4|Fashion illustration.description: This is a fashion illustration, likely a print or lithograph, depicting a woman in a long, flowing evening gown with a colorful, abstract floral pattern. Année 1924 Planche 58", and "Modèle déposé. Reproduction interdite." The woman's face is stylized and not clearly identifiable as a specific real person.

I.3|masterclass-5|File:AK ER Exhibition.description: This is a promotional poster or flyer, likely a digital print or graphic design, featuring a photograph of a person in a black coat walking on a city street.
